papers.title: Increased CCR2-immunopositive myeloid cells in the putamen and cerebellar white matter with blood-brain barrier disruption in multiple system atrophy.
papers.abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction. Recently, a close relationship of neuroinflammation to MSA pathogenesis was identified. Studies in mouse models of MSA have indicated that peripheral-type myeloid cells and endogenous microglia promote neuroinflammation in MSA. However, their distinct roles in MSA pathogenesis remain unknown. We performed immunohistochemical analyses of brain tissues obtained at autopsy from patients with MSA and age-matched controls to examine the putamen and cerebellar white matter with antibodies against CCR2 (a chemokine receptor expressed by monocyte-lineage cells), TMEM119 for microglia, and fibrinogen for blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage. The CCR2-immunopositive area was significantly increased in both regions in MSA patients compared to controls (putamen, p = 0.0043; cerebellar white matter, p = 0.0438); however, the TMEM119-immunopositive area showed no significant between-group difference (putamen, p = 0.4220; cerebellar white matter, p = 0.8152). The densities of CCR2-immunopositive areas in the putamen and cerebellar white matter were positively correlated (Pearson's r = 0.7325, p = 0.0248). In the putamen, fibrinogen immunoreactivity and perivascular leakage were increased and showed a distribution similar to that of CCR2 immunostaining (p = 0.0398). These findings suggest that CCR2-immunopositive myeloid cell accumulation in regions with BBB dysfunction may involve recruitment of peripheral monocyte-lineage cells.

Disruption of paramyosin compromises muscle integrity and alters systemic trehalose metabolism in Helicoverpa armigera.
papers.abstract: Trehalose is a principal circulating sugar in insects, maintaining a critical balance between energy supply and storage through systemic insulin signalling. Among different tissues, insect muscle functions as a metabolic hub, coordinating trehalose utilization and glucose uptake to sustain energy homeostasis. In Helicoverpa armigera, we examined whether paramyosin (key muscle gene) silencing influence carbohydrate metabolism. HaPrm silencing led to muscle defects and delayed pupation, indicating a crucial role of HaPrm in development. Transcriptomics revealed dysregulation of genes involved in carbohydrate metabolism and insulin-mTOR signalling. Notably, expression and enzymatic activities of HaTPS/TPP and HaTreh(s) were reduced in HaPrm-silenced insects, accompanied by their altered metabolite intermediate levels. Given that trehalose metabolism fuels both glycolysis and glycogen synthesis, HaPrm silencing also altered the expression of glycolytic, glycogen metabolism and energy-sensing genes. Metabolomics further demonstrated differential accumulation of intermediates from glycolysis, glycogen recycling, the TCA cycle and amino acid metabolism. Moreover, insulin-mTOR signalling genes and the glucose-sensing transcription factor were significantly affected, highlighting the sensitivity of nutrient-sensing mechanisms to HaPrm silencing. Taken together, these results suggest that HaPrm disruption affects muscle integrity and is linked to changes in insulin-mTOR signalling and trehalose metabolism. These data highlight the close relationship between muscle architecture and energy homeostasis in H. armigera.

papers.title: Neuroprotective eremophilane sesquiterpenoids from Ligularia species attenuate glutamate-induced oxidative stress via MAPK signaling.
papers.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ligularia species (Asteraceae) have long been used in traditional East Asian medicine for the treatment of pain and inflammatory disorders. Although neuroprotection is not among their documented traditional indications, the close relationship among inflammation, oxidative stress, and neuronal injury, together with the reported analgesic and anti-inflammatory activities of these species, provides a rationale for investigating their neuroprotective potential. AIM OF THE STUDY: Eremophilane sesquiterpenoids are the principal and most characteristic constituents of the genus Ligularia, and those from other natural sources have been reported to protect neuronal cells against oxidative stress. Given the close relationship among oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuronal injury, the traditional anti-inflammatory use of Ligularia and the reported neuroprotective activity of eremophilane sesquiterpenoids suggest that the genus may be a source of neuroprotective constituents, which has not yet been investigated. This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the neuroprotective activity and eremophilane sesquiterpenoid profiles of three traditionally used Ligularia species (L. taquetii, L. fischeri, and L. stenocephala), and to identify the active constituents and their underlying mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Neuroprotective activity was assessed in a glutamate-induced HT-22 hippocampal neuronal cell model. Non-targeted UHPLC-Orbitrap MS metabolomics with feature-based molecular networking was used to compare metabolite profiles and to guide isolation. Isolated compounds were structurally characterized by spectroscopic and computational analyses and quantified by validated LC-MS/MS. Intracellular ROS and Ca2+ levels, along with the expression of apoptosis-related and MAPK proteins, were measured, complemented by network pharmacology, molecular docking, and a Caenorhabditis elegans 6-hydroxydopamine model. papers.title: Participant experiences of stopping ART as part of a clinical trial; findings from a qualitative study within the RIO trial in the United Kingdom.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evaluation of the efficacy of immunotherapeutic strategies aimed at achieving durable antiretroviral treatment (ART)-free control within a clinical trial relies on analytical treatment interruptions (ATIs). ATIs involve stopping ART to assess post-intervention efficacy with frequent viral load monitoring. These trials rely on participant commitment but also involve uncertainty about the timing and experience of viral rebound, transmission risk, and impacts on personal and sexual relationships. Understanding participants' lived experiences is critical to participant involvement and retention and to designing ATI studies that are ethical, feasible, and acceptable. METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study involving semi-structured interviews with 20 cisgender men living with HIV enroled in the phase 2 double-blinded randomised placebo-controlled RIO trial of HIV-specific broadly neutralising antibodies between January and May 2025 in the United Kingdom. We transcribed, coded and analysed the interviews using thematic analysis. RESULTS: The participants described being motivated by scientific altruism but had worries about stopping ART. During the ATI, participants found breaking their daily pill-taking routine challenging, yet a majority described feelings of liberation thereafter. The participants preferred once weekly viral load testing, as it reassured safety, which was coupled with support from researchers, who buffered anxiety during periods of viral rebound. ATIs had a notable impact on personal relationships, including avoidance of dating, reduced intimacy and sexual pleasure while off ART. Easy access for partners without HIV to free PrEP, PEP, and condoms was welcomed by all participants. Restarting ART was difficult following the ATI, but was resolved with pre-trial preparation supporting adherence. papers.title: [Home(s) inside and out-Artistic self-representations by psychiatric inpatients around 1900].
papers.abstract: Around 1900, what did "home" mean to people who, marginalized from the rest of civil society, were permanently confined within psychiatric institutions? Where did they feel they belonged (emotionally); did memories of family, landscape and politically defined territories dominate or was it the appropriation of the institutional space? An exploration of the Heidelberg Prinzhorn Collection, a collection unique in the world, provides a multifaceted answer to these questions. The historical collection contains paintings, drawings, texts, sculptures and musical compositions by psychiatric patients from institutions in German-speaking countries dating from around 1840 to the Nazi era.An interdisciplinary research project at the intersection of art history and the history of psychiatry, based at the Heidelberg Special Research Field (SFB) 1671 "Home(s). Phenomena-Practices-Representations", aims to re-examine the phenomenon of institutional psychiatry from its subjective, emotional perspective by focusing on "Home(s)" or "Heimat(en)". Based on the works and other sources it explores the motives of patient artists in the context of (the search for) affiliation, taking as its starting point the situation of exclusion from conventional "homely" connections. The examination of their artistic strategies is also conducted on the assumption that it will enable statements to be made about notions of home and affiliation within the "matrix" of mainstream society from which the patient-artists originated. This essay presents the initial findings based on three examples of different historical approaches to the subject. Was bedeutete um 1900 „Heimat“ für Menschen, die, aus der übrigen Zivilgesellschaft ausgegrenzt, dauerhaft in psychiatrischen Anstalten untergebracht waren? papers.title: Low-Temperature Demulsification-Induced Gelation Coupled With Gel-Confined Freeze Casting for Highly Elastic Conductive Aerogels in Wireless Gait Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Polymer-based conductive aerogels are promising for flexible piezoresistive sensors but suffer from skeleton deformation and conductive filler detachment under high-strain and long-term compression. Here, an aminopropyltriethoxysilane/carboxylated carbon nanotubes/waterborne polyurethane (APTS/CNTs/WPU) aerogel featuring a semi-interpenetrating network is developed through a strategy combining low-temperature demulsification-induced gelation with gel-confined freeze-casting and simultaneously possesses a highly elastic skeleton, continuous conductive pathways, and reinforced filler/matrix interfaces. The low-temperature condition retards the electrostatic demulsification rate between anionic WPU and protonated APTS, transforming the otherwise rapidly destabilizing emulsion into a controllable gelation process. Accompanied by the gradual occurrence of electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and hydrolysis-condensation reactions of silane, a semi-interpenetrating gel network is established within minutes. The formed gel network prevents re-agglomeration of CNTs and ensures their stable immobilization within the skeleton during freeze-casting. The aerogel exhibits 99.1% elastic recovery after 10 cycles at 80% strain and 5.1% plastic deformation after 10 000 cycles. The piezoresistive sensor achieves a detection range of 0-408 kPa, a maximum sensitivity of 12.33 kPa-1, and stable response over 10 000 cycles. Furthermore, a sensing array integrated with a wireless/wired signal acquisition system is constructed for monitoring gait pressure distribution, fully demonstrating its substantial application potential in human motion perception and wearable electronics.

papers.title: Stabilizing Water Molecules in Hydrogel Electrolytes Enables 2.8 V-Class Purely Aqueous Zn-Li Hybrid Batteries.
papers.abstract: Currently, reported high-voltage aqueous zinc batteries generally operate below 2.0 V. Achieving a discharge plateau/average operating voltage exceeding 2.0 V typically requires charging voltages above 2.5 V; however, the limited electrochemical stability of water molecules in has thus far prevented purely aqueous zinc batteries from reaching this threshold. Here, we report an extreme water-confinement strategy that elevates the oxygen evolution potential of water in a poly(acrylamide-co-hydroxypropyl acrylate) hydrogel electrolyte to 2.85 V versus Zn/Zn2+, far beyond the theoretical value (∼1.58 V versus Zn/Zn2+). This remarkable enhancement originates from the synergistic effects of strong cation-water coordination, TFSI--induced water segregation, and extensive hydrogen bonding within the polymer network, which collectively suppress water activity. When coupled with a lithium nickel manganese oxide cathode, the hydrogel electrolyte enables a 2.8 V-class Zn-Li hybrid battery that delivers a record-breaking average operating voltage/discharge plateau of 2.35 V, far exceeding all previously reported purely aqueous zinc batteries. The battery further exhibits excellent mechanical robustness and directly powers a multifunctional wireless sensing monitoring of dynamic pressure, finger movement, muscle activity, speech, and full-body motion. This work provides a viable pathway toward ultrahigh-voltage aqueous zinc batteries for next-generation wearable and intelligent electronic systems.

papers.title: Parenting Experience and Family Dynamics Among Parents of Children With Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to examine the associations between family dynamics and parenting experiences among parents of children with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). METHOD: A cross-sectional survey was conducted using convenience sampling among 341 parents of children with NDDs recruited from special education institutions and public healthcare facilities. Data were collected via an online questionnaire comprising the Parenting Stress Index-Short Form, Parenting Sense of Competence Scale, Parental Bonding Instrument, Family Adaptation Partnership Growth Affection Resolve Questionnaire, and Family Closeness and Adaptability Scale. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression were performed to examine interrelationships among variables. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors. RESULT: A total of 341 parents participated, reporting on children primarily diagnosed with developmental delay (DD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disabilities (ID). Correlation analyses revealed significant negative relationships between parenting stress and parenting style (r = -0.626, p < 0.01), family functioning (r = -0.831, p < 0.01), and family setting (r = -0.792, p < 0.01). Hierarchical regression analyses demonstrated that parenting style (β = -0.159 to -0.157, p < 0.001), family functioning (β = -0.746, p < 0.001), and family setting (β = - 0.733, p < 0.001) were significant negative predictors of parenting stress. A suppression effect was observed for parenting efficacy, which emerged as a significant positive predictor (β = 0.097 to 0.182, p < 0.01) only after accounting for family-level variables. papers.title: Chemical proximity governs open-world infrared identification of microplastics using dual-evidence calibration.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) classifiers can assign familiar polymer labels to spectra outside their training domain. We developed SPARC-FTIR to couple class-conditional conformal prediction with a calibrated distance gate for binary high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP) identification with rejection. Five spectral views were combined in a training-derived principal-component representation. The two gates distinguished label-set uncertainty from departure from the known feature domain and produced four evidence states. After auditing sample identifiers, 776 spectra were retained from an open ATR-FTIR collection; 689 HDPE/PP spectra supported training, calibration and testing, while 87 non-target spectra were withheld. On the primary test partition, closed-set balanced accuracy was 100%, 124 of 139 known spectra were accepted correctly, and 37 of 87 unknown spectra were rejected. Rejection was 29.4% for low-density polyethylene, 33.3% for mixtures and 100% for the 14 remaining unknown spectra. Across 30 group-preserving splits, mean known acceptance and unknown rejection were 92.8% and 36.3%, respectively. Matched spectral-library comparisons showed different subgroup trade-offs in acceptance and rejection. Frozen-model evaluation on two additional libraries showed acquisition-dependent acceptance and rejection. The calibrated decision states provide an auditable basis for reviewing spectra within a declared HDPE/PP scope; overlapping polyolefin spectra and cross-library transfer remain the principal constraints.

papers.title: Predicting treatment recovery and adherence in alcohol behavioral couple therapy using natural language processing.
papers.journal: Journal of substance use and addiction treatment
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alcohol Behavioral Couple Therapy (ABCT) is an efficacious treatment for Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). Research increasingly focuses on identifying predictors of treatment outcomes to guide the continued refinement of ABCT for diverse AUD populations and relationship typologies, with language spoken by couples emerging as a promising behavioral domain for understanding treatment success. Leveraging natural language processing (NLP) methods and a prospective design, the present study examined a broad range of linguistic features exhibited by couples as predictors and moderators of treatment outcomes. METHOD: Participants represent a subset (n = 84, 42 couples) of individuals enrolled in a larger parent study examining ABCT intervention efficacy. Patients' drinking behaviors were tracked throughout treatment and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. Using NLP tools, linguistic features of patients' and partners' speech during session 1 of ABCT were extracted, respectively. RESULTS: Partners' behaviors moderated patients' drinking trajectories, with patients whose partners more frequently referenced alcohol, β = -0.0015, SE = 0.0006, p = 0.0075, and paired alcohol-related statements with positive sentiment, β = -0.0717, SE = 0.0183, p < 0.001, reporting more pronounced declines in drinking quantity over time. After accounting for patients' effects, patients whose partners used more collective pronouns showed more pronounced declines in drinking frequency over time, β = -0.0140, SE = 0.0060, p = 0.0204. papers.title: Development and Evaluation of a Trauma-Informed Women's Health Education Program for Intimate Partner Violence Survivors: A Mixed-Methods Study.
papers.abstract: Women with a history of intimate partner violence (IPV) are at increased risk for cardiovascular disease, human papillomavirus (HPV), cervical cancer, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which we collectively termed women's health issues (WHIs). This study aimed to educate IPV survivors through a trauma-informed, WHI education program tailored to the needs and experiences of IPV victims, based on focus group data. An education program was created using data from 10 focus groups (n = 38), and these interactive presentations on WHIs were presented to IPV survivors (n = 69). Participants completed demographic surveys, including questions about physician acknowledgment of IPV as a risk factor for chronic conditions, and pre-post tests to evaluate the effectiveness of the educational sessions. Education session data revealed that 39% of participants had never heard of HPV, 38% had not received a Pap smear in the last 3 years, and 15% did not know where to get tested for HIV. Only 15% (n = 10) of participants reported that their physician acknowledged IPV as a risk factor for disease. Following the health education, there was a significant normalized gain of 55.66%, with paired t tests comparing pretest/posttest scores supporting understanding of WHIs (p < .01). Tailored education modules about WHIs proved effective in educating women who have experienced IPV. Future iterations will focus on topics informed by participant responses, such as diabetes mellitus, neurological disorders, reproductive health, and gastrointestinal diseases. This study opens avenues for further exploration of the connection between IPV and health initiatives.

papers.title: Fifty years of elder abuse research: what have we learned about risk, assessment, prevention, and treatment?
papers.abstract: Elder abuse has been a focus of research and policy for over half a century. This article discusses this history, Focusing on elder abuse in the community, we trace seminal studies and innovative research and policy efforts that have sought to address key elder abuse questions, including how prevalent elder abuse is, why it occurs, risk and protective factors, and what is known about how it can be prevented/addressed. Although reviews indicate that effective interventions are lacking, we discuss several promising approaches at the program and organizational level. We recommend building on approaches from child maltreatment and intimate partner violence, including applying risk assessments that offer important lessons for elder abuse. We conclude by recommending refinement of assessments to identify different types of risks, along with interventions that recognize different etiologies and treatment approaches.

papers.title: The association between intimate partner violence exposure and post-traumatic stress symptoms among clinical nurses in Guangdong province: Sequential indirect associations through psychological resilience and emotional exhaustion: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is associated with adverse psychological outcomes, but evidence on post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) among clinical nurses remains limited. This study examined the association between IPV exposure and PTSS among clinical nurses in Guangdong Province, China, and assessed sequential indirect associations involving psychological resilience and emotional exhaustion. Data were collected from 438 clinical nurses recruited from 5 tertiary-level general hospitals in Guangdong Province, China, using a general information questionnaire, the Short Form of the Revised Conflict Tactics Scales, the 10-item Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, the Emotional Exhaustion Scale, and the post-traumatic stress disorder checklist for DSM-5 Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition. Analyses included independent-sample t tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlations, multiple linear regression, and path analysis. Mean scores for PTSS, IPV exposure, psychological resilience, and emotional exhaustion were 29.41 ± 16.21, 17.28 ± 8.70, 25.28 ± 6.16, and 21.95 ± 10.06, respectively. IPV exposure was positively correlated with PTSS (r = 0.740, P < .001) and emotional exhaustion (r = 0.776, P < .001), and negatively correlated with psychological resilience (r = -0.733, P < .001). Psychological resilience was negatively correlated with PTSS (r = -0.767, P < .001) and emotional exhaustion (r = -0.803, P < .001), while emotional exhaustion was positively correlated with PTSS (r = 0.764, P < .001). papers.title: Population-level effects of a community-based program on intimate partner violence: A stepped-wedge trial in South African informal settlements.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a widespread challenge in informal settlements, where poverty and unemployment are prevalent. The evidence for strategies to reduce IPV at the population level in such settings is limited. A stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial was conducted in 18 informal settlements in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, to evaluate the Asibonisane Community Responses (CR) program. The program included a ten-session Stepping Stones curriculum and community-wide HIV and IPV education. Four survey rounds were implemented with population-based samples of men aged 18-35 and women aged 18-24. The analytic sample comprised 549 women and 438 men in primary partnerships interviewed at least twice. At baseline, 22.8% of women reported physical IPV, 11.4% sexual IPV, and 21.3% emotional IPV; among men, 15.9% reported physical perpetration, 3.8% sexual, and 9.2% emotional. Intention-to-treat analysis showed significant reductions among women in emotional (aOR = 0.42, p < .001), physical (aOR = 0.70, p < .05), and sexual IPV (aOR = 0.27, p < .001), with similar reductions in the number and frequency of violent acts. Men reported decreases in emotional and physical IPV perpetration, though not sexual IPV. The findings demonstrate that multi-session community programming can reduce IPV in high-prevalence contexts, and that detailed tracking of multiple IPV forms helps capture meaningful progress toward population-level violence reduction.
